title: CausalDub
subtitle: Replacement-Aware Video Dubbing for Diverse Sources
summary: CausalDub learns a full-context replacement response with valid asymmetric supervision, transfers it to a two-evaluation causal editor, and bounds generated-state propagation with source-reanchored windows.

domains.name: HDTF
domains.description: Studio and interview footage with replacement speech.

domains.name: TalkVid
domains.description: Web-video appearance, motion, and recording conditions.

domains.name: CausalDub-Bench
domains.description: Source-disjoint generated speakers shown in the benchmark's 512×512 stable evaluation crops.

comparisons.title: CausalDub-Bench
comparisons.description: The four methods receive the same source clip and replacement speech. The source is included only as a visual reference.

comparisons.title: HDTF
comparisons.description: The four methods receive the same captured source and replacement speech, exposing synchronization and source-preservation differences.

ablations.title: Reconstruction alone is not replacement control
ablations.description: Matched teacher checkpoints on HDTF-30, TalkVid-50, CausalDub-50, and VoxCeleb2-30. Replacement-aware refinement raises cross-audio Sync-C by 0.954–1.653; mixed FVD changes do not support a universal fidelity claim.

ablations.title: DMD recovers compression-induced quality loss
ablations.description: On the frozen 256-source development split, two-step trajectory regression raises FVD from 8.91 to 10.84; distribution matching lowers it to 7.76. These are single-seed stage diagnostics, so DMD is claimed only as quality recovery.

long_form.title: Long execution exposes what short clips hide
long_form.description: Six complete 60-second cases demonstrate source-reanchored execution. Pair 14 additionally compares public baselines and the continuous-cache control under the same source and replacement speech.

limitations: SyncNet confidence is not treated as proof of phoneme correctness; independent recognition is reported separately.
Source-reanchored 60-second execution does not establish drift-free persistent generation.
The benchmark does not cover arbitrary generator out-of-distribution behavior or universal fidelity superiority.
